details:
Project overview

Mars Explorer is an interactive 3D experience that lets people explore a Mars-inspired landscape from a rover-height, first-person view. Built with Three.js, it uses Mars imagery as visual reference for the terrain, rocks, cliffs, and sky. Visitors can look around, move through the scene, and travel between exploration points using a map-style interface. An optional voice guide can explain locations and respond to simple navigation questions.

Benefits and intended impact

The project makes Mars exploration more approachable and engaging. It gives students and the public an opportunity to experience a Martian landscape interactively, rather than only viewing it in still images. The intended impact is to spark curiosity about Mars, encourage learning about planetary science, and make space exploration feel more accessible.

Tools and development

The project is designed with Three.js for 3D graphics and JavaScript, HTML, and CSS for the interactive experience and interface. It draws on the team’s supplied Mars images as visual references. Browser speech features can support optional voice input and spoken responses where available.

Creativity and design considerations

The creative idea is to bring together a first-person rover experience, map-style navigation, Mars-inspired visuals, and a conversational guide. The team considered ease of use, clear navigation, accessibility, performance on typical devices, and how to distinguish NASA imagery and established facts from generated demo terrain. The experience is a visual exploration demo, not a scientifically accurate map of Mars.
